evidence.claim: The TSE said Lula won the second round of the 2022 presidential election with 50.83% of valid votes against Bolsonaro's 49.17%, and that Bolsonaro was the incumbent president who had sought reelection.
evidence.title: Lula é eleito novamente presidente da República do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The TSE said Lula won the second round of the 2022 presidential election with 50.83% of valid votes against Bolsonaro's 49.17%, and that Bolsonaro was the incumbent president who had sought reelection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary election authority record with official result totals.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Bolsonaro's contestability and transfer-of-power obligation.
contrary_evidence: This proves turnover occurred, but not that Bolsonaro himself accepted it promptly or in good faith.

evidence.claim: The TSE said no fraud had been documented since electronic voting began in 1996, noted that the system had elected multiple presidents including Bolsonaro, and stated that the process had permitted alternation in power.
evidence.title: Nota à imprensa
evidence.excerpt: The TSE said no fraud had been documented since electronic voting began in 1996, noted that the system had elected multiple presidents including Bolsonaro, and stated that the process had permitted alternation in power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary court/election authority statement responding directly to Bolsonaro's fraud allegations.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited baseline relevant to the 2022 campaign and post-election dispute.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's repeated fraud narrative, though the statement itself is institutional.
contrary_evidence: It is a court rebuttal, not an independent empirical audit of every election claim.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said disinformation amplified by Bolsonaro and his allies flooded the online landscape ahead of the October 2022 election, that Bolsonaro had made at least 6,000 false or misleading statements by August 2022, and that those claims were reproduced through official channels and social media as an organized disinformation machine.
evidence.title: Brazil: Freedom on the Net 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said disinformation amplified by Bolsonaro and his allies flooded the online landscape ahead of the October 2022 election, that Bolsonaro had made at least 6,000 false or misleading statements by August 2022, and that those claims were reproduced through official channels and social media as an organized disinformation machine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major independent monitoring report with detailed 2022 case coverage and attribution to Bolsonaro and allies.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro attribution for the statements and the political network around them.
contrary_evidence: Freedom House is an advocacy/monitoring source and may emphasize harms more than institutional defenses.

evidence.claim: The TSE said the authenticity test proved the official election-system software was installed in the electronic voting machines and that the test was public, real-time, and conducted before voting began.
evidence.title: Justiça Eleitoral realiza Teste de Autenticidade dos Sistemas Eleitorais antes da votação
evidence.excerpt: The TSE said the authenticity test proved the official election-system software was installed in the electronic voting machines and that the test was public, real-time, and conducted before voting began.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary election-authority description of the audit procedure in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional counterweight to Bolsonaro's fraud narrative rather than a Bolsonaro action.
contrary_evidence: This demonstrates institutional resilience, not Bolsonaro's own commitment to that resilience.

evidence.claim: The TSE said the first round of the 2022 election and the days after it were marked by intense proliferation of fake news about the electoral process, and that the court and partner fact-checkers debunked the main false claims.
evidence.title: Fato ou Boato: Justiça Eleitoral desmentiu as principais fake news sobre o processo eleitoral em 2022
evidence.excerpt: The TSE said the first round of the 2022 election and the days after it were marked by intense proliferation of fake news about the electoral process, and that the court and partner fact-checkers debunked the main false claims.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary election-authority article directly describing the 2022 misinformation wave and its rebuttal.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The misinformation environment is Bolsonaro-linked, though the article itself is about election administration response.
contrary_evidence: This is institutional-response evidence, not direct evidence of Bolsonaro personally authoring each falsehood.
